Scope: collector and local roads, potable water, sewage, storm drainage, irrigation, TSE, medium voltage, street lighting and telecom networks, a sewage pump station, storm drainage ponds, the boundary fence and guard room, and utility buildings, in the 2nd Industrial City in Dammam.

Status at a glance

Progress is measured as physical % complete, weighted by budgeted man-hours. The weekly report (WPR-42, Rev.2026.1) gives 42.89% actual against 63.95% planned in the revised plan; the original baseline in its weekly chart sheet gives 82.94% planned. This week the project gained 2.36% (447 man-days) against 3.20% planned.

The forecast delay grew to 131 days. The weekly report and the P6 update now both forecast completion on 03-Jul-2027, against the contract date of 22-Feb-2027; the completion milestone has −100.25 days of float in P6 (−95.5 last week). Sewage pipes reached 1,868 m (90.1%) and potable water 1,450 m (61.5%, from 390 m), but the weekly report still gives 1,207 m for storm drainage. To finish on 22-Feb-2027 the remaining 57.11% must be done in 12 weeks, about 4.76% a week, against 2.36% achieved this week.

Data notes

  • Only the Rev.2026.1 version of WPR-42 was uploaded (last week there were two versions). Its Major Quantities sheet is identical to WPR-41's, so the fence and building quantities are not updated; the quantities section uses the Conclusion sheet only.
  • Week number: WPR-42 states "Current Contract Weeks: 48 of 61", and (24-Nov-2026 − 23-Dec-2025) ÷ 7 = 336 days gives week 48 as well.
  • Weekly gain: the cover sheet gives 433 man-days (2.28%) earned this week, but cumulative earned rose from 7,697 to 8,144 man-days, i.e. 447 (2.36%); the weekly column leaves out the 14 man-days gained in procurement. This report uses 2.36%, which the weekly chart sheet also gives.
  • Testing and commissioning shows 101 man-days earned (5.3%) with nothing planned, and no network is complete yet. It accounts for 0.53% of this week's 2.36% gain; the basis should be confirmed.
  • Baseline: the cover sheet no longer gives a baseline physical plan; 82.94% is from the weekly chart sheet (106,488 baseline man-hours). The chart sheet's revised plan (64.49%) differs from the cover (63.95%). There is no monthly chart sheet, so the S-curve uses the last weekly point of each month.
  • Storm drainage: the Conclusion sheet still gives 1,207 m (unchanged for two weeks) although the phase earned 97 man-days; the MODON follow-up dashboard gives 2,962 m. The dashboard also gives a sewage total of 2,027 m (WPR-42: 2,073 m).
  • Road earthworks rose by 163,190 m³ in one week (637,536 to 800,726 m³) while the roads phase earned only 13 man-days.
  • Procurement tracker: the file dated 24-Nov-2026 is byte-identical to the one dated 17-Nov-2026, which matched the one of 03-Nov-2026. Several items still say "delivery in mid-November" with 0 delivered, and some expected delivery dates are in December 2027 or in the past.
  • The MODON follow-up dashboard (file still named 10-11-2026 but dated 24-Nov-2026) still shows 421 workers, 156 pieces of equipment and 14,369,702 SAR from 3 invoices, which match neither WPR-42 (278, 119, 17,837,089.43 SAR from 4 approved invoices).
  • Invoices: the cover gives 14 submitted invoices while the log lists 4. The log still references DAMT-02-001 and a revised contract value of 21,100,000.
  • Quality: FIR, MIR and NCR counts are exactly as last week although work continued on site. The HSE sheet still carries project ID DAMT-02-001 and report number 41 beside 42.
  • Milestones: the weekly report's "latest plan" dates are still earlier than the baseline for most networks, and milestones 2 to 4 are marked as forecast although P6 records them as complete.
  • Issues: the weekly report still shows 20-Apr-2026 as the expected closure of the land dispute, while the R&I register moved it to 20-Dec-2026.
  • The contractor checklist is still named "WPR41 … 17-11-2026" although it is for WPR-42, and it marks all 42 items as done.
  • Photos: 18 of the 25 photos are the same files as last week. The seven new ones have no date, GPS stamp or EXIF data.
  • The Financial Progress sheet gives cost-based progress; it is not used in this report.
